subject.title: [Bug]:  Isolated cron session agent loop continues consuming tokens after run marked "ok"

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: The direct closing PR and the competing strict-validation PR encode opposite public cron semantics, and the choice affects existing persisted jobs, user cost exposure, and session-state retention.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Land the cleanup-by-default direction only after it covers already-persisted omitted isolated recurring jobs and preserves explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Adopt one-shot-only delete-after-run
options.body: Continue through the strict-validation path and reconcile UI, Gateway errors, docs, and operator recovery before closing this issue.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only default
options.body: Land the new-job default while documenting that existing omitted jobs require operator action or a separate migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Land the cleanup-by-default direction only after it covers already-persisted omitted isolated recurring jobs and preserves explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans cron defaults, persisted-job compatibility, and product cleanup policy, which matches the recent cron normalization/store history.
